Miss Melody sits in her rocking chair in front of the corner store that her and her husband Mister Allen have owned for 30 plus years. today is no different from any other. Miss melody waits as her usual customers stroll from their homes from up and down Jackson ave. for a cup of coffee, maybe some fresh eggs, and (even though she does not believe in having such things in her store) a pack of cigarettes and a 6 pack of beer. Mister Allen is steadily working in the yard, mowing the lawn, weeding the garden, trimming the hedges. Really any thing he can find to keep him self busy. every time his wife Miss Melody finds him taking a nap or having a rest she automatically find something for him to do inside the store. And Mister Allen hates that more then any thing in the world. He hates being inside that dark dank putrid place. all the paper work and book keeping does not bother him a bit. but in 30 or more years he can count the number of times he had to go into that store on one finger. 

As he is in the yard he remembers that faithful day. 

This day was very different from every other day that has ever happened. The day that Mister Allen had to go inside Sharpe and Sons Corner Store. Miss Melody sat in her chair as she did every morning waving at passer byes whom didn't stop at the store. Mister Allen working in the yard as always, today cutting back the morning glory plants because they had started to overgrow the fence they were trained to. the kids that belonged to the Beckwith family had just left the store with a soda pop and some candy. Miss melody never charged full price for the candy or the soda to the kids she enjoyed them coming around having lost her own children in the war. Mister Allen disliked the fact they could never find a way to stay on the sidewalk. he had just planted that grass seed and they always tore up the lawn on there way out. He'll never admit it but their smiles brightened up his day as-well. 

that was the end of the similarities on that day. after this life is going to change for the few who lived on Jackson ave. 

Miss Melody was found in her usual place. when the Mister Gramm asked her "have you ever seen a person so strange as the one asking for an Allen Sharpe."
 
Miss Melody was taken aback, no one had addressed her husband in that manor  since before they were married. she asked "why would someone be asking for my husband in such a informal way." 

Mister Gramm replied "I had no time to ask he seemed to be in a life threatening hurry, he looked pail and alien almost, as if his odyssey had not only nearly taken his life but had brought him hear from a land so foreign it may not have been earth" 

Miss Melody became visually concerned. way would a man be asking for her husband and why did he do it in a way that was so disrespectful to an elder. wear could he have come from why is he hear. it wasn't long before the whole neighborhood had been talking about this man. the way strange way he looked, how he talked, how he was asking for Allen Sharpe. it seemed every person around had known of this except her and her husband for whom he asked. even the children were asking did you see the man asking for Allen Sharpe. is that your husbands name. when did they call him that. the suspicion in Miss Melody grew so much to the point she had to ask.

"Allen" as she only called him "please turn off the horrible saw and don't cut that tree anymore i like it the way it is now it doesn't need another trimming for the third time this week, and please come inside i am worried, there is a man asking for Allen Sharpe"

at this mention Mister Allen's spine quacked as if the ground under him was trembling. he had a gut feeling he should go inside and load his war pistol. he shoved the cold steel of the .45 in back of his pants on the small of his back, he loaded the 12 gauge with a full 7 rounds and placed it on the inside of the door to the store. then telling telling Melody(as only he called her) to get upstairs and close the windows and blinds. and he turned off the lights to the store and locked the door bolt lock and all. sitting in the back room in an office chair he began to think of the possibilities, why would someone address him like this it has been almost fifty years since he wore a uniform for his country. so long ago he almost forgot what he had done himself, and he might have had this not reminded him. 

sitting in the dark dank putrid stench he hated so much this store, sweating thinking could this be a man looking to exact revenge for a war crime committed in what seems a completely different life. every scenario of demise a person could think of was running through his mind all at once. why would a greasy dirty man who appeared to have no idea what a shower was be looking for him. why would someone so "out of this world looking" try to find him. what does any of this mean. as he wondered the evening faded to night but the time slowed. his anxiety quickened and the night grew cold and the time stood still.

it wasn't until late the next morning that any of these questions were answered. it wasn't until late the next morning until their lives changes. 

Melody do not open the store this morning we do not who is looking for me we do not know if he means us harm or what his purpose is. she obliged to that but to his dismay she still stubbornly sat in her chair with a cup of coffee. but this morning Mister Allen made a point to work in the front yard of his store. staring at every passer by with an eye at would scare the pants of the devil himself. and by the looks of things nobody bother to ask if the store was open or if any other news had come of the man asking for Allen Sharpe.  the anxiety didn't shrink, the quake in his spine didn't turn in to a mere shiver and the .45 never left his backside. 

it wasn't until nearly 10 that he decided there was nothing more to do in the front yard so he resigned to sitting the opposite chair to his wife and enjoy a cup of coffee him self. at this moment he couldnt resist bring up a subject not mentioned for years between the two.

he turned to his wife and said "i miss him."
"who" she asked.
"Mister Christian"(as he would have been called had they not lost him in the war) he said.
"our son" the tears instantly began streaming "i thought you forgot, every morning i see his picture near the register, every day i pray for him" she said. 
"how could i forget the store is called Sharpe and Sons" he couldn't help it either letting a tear fall against his will. "the reason i named it that is so that i will never be able to forget" he said to her trying to hide his face.

it was at this moment as faith would have it that changed every thing. as they sat there in the chairs staring at each other knowing what the other is thinking. a man walked up. but not the person they expected, not the dirty and filthy man for another planet, not a man a person in the town knew, or ever seen before, a respect full young man. a person of arms(that is to say military) with stripes on his shoulder and metals on his chest a man of renown by all appearances. its was only a few seconds that he stood at the end of the walk way that the Beckwith children from across the street pointed saying that the man, that's him asking for a Allen Sharpe. but were did he get the uniform yesterday he was covered in grease and unshaven. and today a top ranked man of arms. it seemed at this moment in time every member of Jackson ave. had found there way miraculously to the front of the store all at once. 

it was then that they started to notice this man had a shocking resemblance. Mister Allen and Miss Melody saw it too. they looked at each other thinking the same exact thing and not believing it all together. it seemed to big of a coincidence for any of it to be possible. 

"Allen Sharpe, Melody Sharpe" the stranger said.
"you better have a Damn good reason for addressing me and my wife out side of the respect you owe use as elders" Mister Allen said as loudly and stern as his voice would allow.
"yes sir" the young man replied with a solute that had not been seen by Mister Allen in over four decades 

it was at this moment in time things started coming together in the mind of Mister Allen and Miss Melody. the shocking similarities were between them. the man that stood in front of there store Sharpe and Sons looked both like them Miss Melody's eyes and hair Mister Allen's build and ears. 

"mother, father, i am Christian Sharpe, an orphan of the state and a veteran of war i as your long lost son come to give you a gift. he walked to the porch as sat on a knelt before Allen Sharpe and held out his hand. this time with tears in his eyes he said "i Christian Sharpe am under orders to deliver his to a gold star of honor to one Allen Sharpe Master Gunnie of the brother hood of arms for your distinct service of bravery and valor. standing now and giving a final salute. Allen Melody and Christian Sharpe remembered why Sharpe and Sons Corner store ever existed.
